pill.desc: white lyophilized powder in a single-dose vial

clues.kinetics: Its elimination is partly dependent on its receptor on platelets, so patients with high platelet counts have low serum concentrations.
clues.substance: Supplied as a sterile lyophilized powder, reconstituted with sterile water to a concentration of 500 mcg/mL.
clues.product: Approved under a BLA in 125, 250 and 500 mcg single-dose vials, given once weekly.
clues.safety: No boxed warning and no contraindications. Headache is the most commonly reported adverse reaction versus placebo; in children, contusion is among the most common.
clues.indication: Immune thrombocytopenia that has not responded to corticosteroids, immunoglobulins or splenectomy, and survival after acute exposure to myelosuppressive radiation.
clues.mechanism: Binds and activates the TPO receptor, increasing platelet production by a mechanism analogous to endogenous TPO.

tell: A peptibody that activates the TPO receptor; its serum levels fall when platelet counts are high.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak serum concentrations of romiplostim were observed about 7 to 50 hours post dose (median: 14 hours)
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: half-life values ranging from 1 to 34 days (median: 3.5 days)

evidence.biologic: The peptibody molecule contains two identical single-chain subunits, each consisting of human immunoglobulin IgG1 Fc domain
